Natural predators and Monsters roam the astral depths, while lone wanderers of the ancient Maer Lore bear rare witness to a once great civilization.

GLOBAL.AstralMonstersLoreConcept.name: Astral Sea Monsters
GLOBAL.AstralMonstersLoreConcept.description: Astral Sea Monsters are denizens of the Astral Sea Lore. These mana-hungry creatures come in a variety of shapes, from the jellyfish like Astral Syphoner to the horrifically tragic Lost Wizard Lore. They are all designed to thrive in the harsh environment of the Astral Sea, with many leeching life from any traveler caught unaware. However, not all Astral Sea creatures are malevolent, as the gentle Maer Lore are prove.

GLOBAL.AstralVoidLoreConcept.name: Astral Void
GLOBAL.AstralVoidLoreConcept.description: Beyond the reach of the Astral Sea Lore lies the Astral Void, a place where the Astral Flows Lore do not reach, a place of nothingness. A wizard may be banished and cast into the Void, where they drift around until they either manage to find a flow leading them back to a safe place or succumb to the Shadow Trial Lore and perish as one of the Lost Wizard Lore.

GLOBAL.AstralVortexLoreConcept.name: Astral Vortex
GLOBAL.AstralVortexLoreConcept.description: Sometimes the Astral Flows Lore converge into astral vortices, paradoxical culminations of magic energy that bend all meaning of time and space. When entered by beings powerful enough to withstand their shearing forces, they may be used to traverse large distances within the Astral Sea Lore. However, many prefer the use of the much safer—but also rarer—World Gate Lore.

GLOBAL.AthlaLoreConcept.name: Athla
GLOBAL.AthlaLoreConcept.description: Athla is one of the oldest Worlds Within Lore the Astral Sea Lore with a potent convergence of Astral Flows Lore. It is the home to the Valleyof Wonders Lore and Inioch's court. Through the ages Athla has played a pivotal role in events that shaped the cosmos, be it as a realm to conquer, a scene of cosmic battles, or the origin of powerful beings. Many known Godir Lore originate from this world.

GLOBAL.AuldwealdLoreConcept.name: Auldweald
GLOBAL.AuldwealdLoreConcept.description: Auldweald is said to be the original homeworld of the First Elves, from where they first traveled to other Worlds in the Astral Sea Lore. Many elven songs idolize its lush valleys and evergreen forests, and it is said that all elven Souls Lore long to return to this world.

GLOBAL.BloodClanLoreConcept.name: Blood Clan
GLOBAL.BloodClanLoreConcept.description: Often looked down on by the other Giant Clans, the Blood Clan is a conglomeration of any breed of Demigiant imaginable. Loosely organized, the trolls and ogres of the Worlds Within Lore indulge in their savage hierarchies—where for once no actual Giant may boss them around.

GLOBAL.CageOfBindingLoreConcept.name: Cage of Binding
GLOBAL.CageOfBindingLoreConcept.description: For a powerful Godir Lore, who can regularly escape death, there are few things more terrifying than a Cage of Binding. For such an enchanted shell, crafted from rare magic materials, represents the Astral Void Lore and an eternity of nothingness. When sealed inside a Cage of Binding, a Godir Lore will lose their arcane abilities and is rendered completely helpless. However, capturing a Godir Lore inside is no small feat, and only few records in history speak of a wizard unfortunate enough to suffer such a gruesome fate.

GLOBAL.CircleOfDeogaiLoreConcept.name: Circle of Deogai
GLOBAL.CircleOfDeogaiLoreConcept.description:
After the terrible disasters unleashed by the Unmakers Lore, the Archons Lore began to establish the Circles of Deogai throughout the cosmos. They were councils of Godir Lore set on the most disputed worlds, each presided by an Archon arbiter. Through those Circles the Archons fostered stability and monitored the new magics devised by the Wizard King Lore with a watchful eye.

By the time of the Fourth Age, most Circles of Deogai have either been destroyed or dispersed, and the Godir Lore turned to Magehaven Lore as their primary forum of council. Yet some Circles are said to still persist, transformed by the ages until they were given new purpose.

GLOBAL.ColtLoreConcept.name: Company of Lost Treasures
GLOBAL.ColtLoreConcept.description: Renowned for their wealth, the Company of Lost Treasures is extending its influence across the Astral Sea Lore. Specialized in hiring and outfitting skilled adventurers, the Company of Lost Treasures is uncovering and plundering the riches of ancient empires, above all from the ruined jewel of Giant kin, Myrrida Lore. Often accused of shady practices, the officials of the Company have repeatedly proven that their contracts are always honored—one simply must pay attention to all the footnotes.

GLOBAL.CommonwealthLoreConcept.name: Commonwealth
GLOBAL.CommonwealthLoreConcept.description:
The empire of the Commonwealth was initially formed as a joining of races and cultures on Athla Lore, aimed at the sharing of knowledge and the mutual protection of all. While these benign precepts held true for a time, ambition and technological advancement soon outgrew the concepts of the original charter, leading to much strife between factions within and without.

When the World Gates on Athla were reopened the most important figureheads of the Commonwealth, including Edward Portsmith, were defeated or disappeared. In the chaos and under the pressure of returning Wizard Kings, the powerful empire dismantled into factions they once sought to unite.

GLOBAL.CovenantFactionLoreConcept.name: Covenant
GLOBAL.CovenantFactionLoreConcept.description: The Covenant are a faction within the Pantheon of Godir, who seek to uphold ancient agreements of peace and stability, as written by the Archons Lore in ages past. Their lawful tendencies often put them in direct opposition to the Shadrai Faction Lore.

GLOBAL.DemonicOverlordLoreConcept.name: Demonic Overlord
GLOBAL.DemonicOverlordLoreConcept.description:
Few dare speak of them, lest it invite infernal notice or provoke their wrath. The inscrutable masters of the Demonic Regency, and of many Obbadothan horrors besides, Demon Overlords are counted among the mightiest of their kind. Some believe they are ancient fiends ascended through ages of carnage, while others claim they are primordial evils woven into the very fabric of creation.

Whatever their true nature, Demon Overlords are ever eager to bargain. To those deemed worthy, they offer power drawn from the depths of Obbadoth, binding supplicants through pacts both potent and perilous. In this way, they became the unseen architects behind countless infernal covenants that ripple across the Astral Sea.

GLOBAL.DemonicPrinceLoreConcept.name: Demonic Prince
GLOBAL.DemonicPrinceLoreConcept.description:
The Obbadothan Royalty are a loose and ever-shifting assembly bound by infernal pacts. Each member has bargained with a Demon Overlord, trading autonomy for power. As such, entry into the regency is largely open to anyone, or anything willing to make the trade.

Most infamous among them are the Demonic Princes, who, next to their own sinister ambitions, act as the chief commanders of their Overlord across all Worlds Within Lore. Though ever wary that failure—or maliciously twisted pact clause—might see them swiftly supplanted or dragged down screaming into damnation.

GLOBAL.DragonsLoreConcept.name: Dragons
GLOBAL.DragonsLoreConcept.description:
Dragons are among the first creatures that the Allfather Lore gifted with life. The first of these, known as the Elder Dragons, would utilize their vast intelligence and mastery of the elements to aid the Archons in shaping the Worlds within the Astral Sea Lore as well as in crafting powerful artifacts. In all of this, they would be forced to work alongside the Giants Lore, which led to much conflict.

Dragons come in three forms: firstly, the Elder Dragons who were born at the beginning of creation and on occasion ascend to Godirhood through their primal mastery of the arcane arts. Secondly, their offspring, the more common Dragons. Lastly, the far younger and less sophisticated Wyverns, who were hatched in ages since that primordial time. Beyond that, Dragons come in myriad types that are mostly associated with a different element, and some have even been raised as undead versions of their previous selves.

GLOBAL.DreamersLoreConcept.name: Dreamers
GLOBAL.DreamersLoreConcept.description: The origin and nature of the Dreamers is debated with controversy among Godir Lore. Their protectors, the Gloomwatch Lore, claim they are the children of the Allfather Lore and that they were sent to bring an end to Urrath’s corruption. In the records of the Gloomwatch Lore, the Dreamers are attributed with immense creative powers, dreaming creatures, people, and entire worlds into existence. Such pure creation from nothingness is otherwise only observable with The Well Lore, which indeed some beliefs identify as the Allfather Lore.

GLOBAL.DuathaLoreConcept.name: Duatha
GLOBAL.DuathaLoreConcept.description: Duatha, also known as the Fey Realm, is the home world to some of the most notorious creatures. It is a place filled with deception and trickery, where nothing is as it seems and any expectations of common sense can be defied. Those who dare stray into Duatha’s mists are doomed to get lost in it forever—and said to be brought before the realm’s lords, the Duathadae Lore, for judgment.

GLOBAL.DuathadaeLoreConcept.name: Duathadae
GLOBAL.DuathadaeLoreConcept.description:
Shrouds and mysteries surround the Duathadae, lords of the Fey realm Duatha Lore. For all that is known, they are very protective of the lands under their undisputed rule, and their subjects, sometimes capricious, sometimes outright malicious, obey their word, be it through fear or adoration.

There is occasional evidence that their arcane powers may outmatch those of even a Godir Lore, but never have the Duathadae been known to leave their realm Duatha Lore; nor was a Godir Lore to this day foolish enough to challenge them in their own domain.

GLOBAL.ElderVampireLoreConcept.name: Elder Vampire
GLOBAL.ElderVampireLoreConcept.description:
Elder Vampires are ageless undead blessed with nightborn powers, dominating the minds of their thralls and drinking the blood of their enemies. They must shun the sun, but thrive in their Sunless domains spreading from the shadows of their castles.

All Elder Vampires are connected through ancient blood lines, dating back to the Archvampire Lore and the curse of the storied Pale Prince. Due to this, a strong awareness of origin dictates the hierarchies among Vampires and their undead nobility. Still, even an Elder Vampire Hybrid may rise to fame after devouring the power of many Purebloods...

GLOBAL.EldritchSovereignLoreConcept.name: Eldritch Sovereign
GLOBAL.EldritchSovereignLoreConcept.description: Wizards banished to the Astral Void Lore must endure the Shadow Trial Lore. Those that fail the trial lose themselves to madness and become Lost Wizards. Some of these unfortunate souls, however, continue to grow their power until they regain a twisted fraction of sanity as Eldritch Sovereigns. Mangled, shattered, and deconstructed, their powers allow them to pierce the planar veils, unleashing their corrupting ambitions on the worlds. One of their most fearsome talents is their ability to enthrall not just creatures such as Astral Monsters Lore and Shadow Demons Lore, but even entire races to their will.

GLOBAL.ElyaLoreConcept.name: Elya
GLOBAL.ElyaLoreConcept.description: Elya is a young Maer Lore, a mystical species of benevolent Astral Sea Creatures. Unlike many others of her people, Elya feels a strong connection to mortals and the Worlds Within Lore the Astral Sea Lore. Her youth and curiosity bring her closer to Godir Lore - and danger - than any other of her kind would dare.

GLOBAL.EndailonLoreConcept.name: Endailon
GLOBAL.EndailonLoreConcept.description:
The Endailon are powerful cosmic entities from ancient times. They appear to be heavily linked to the Magic Affinities, to the point that some Godir Lore believe that the magic of the cosmos is a manifestation of the Endailon rather than the Endailon being mere manifestations of the affinities themselves.

Emerging myths surround the Endailon, depicting them as the original gods alongside the Allfather Lore who shaped the cosmos and ruled the races throughout. But there is little evidence of the Endailon's motivations and whether or not they concern themselves with the affairs of mortals. In ages past, the Endailon clashed with the Archons, leading to their imprisonment within Grexolis Lore. Now, with the opening of Grexolis Lore, they roam freely again and will leave their mark on the cosmos once more.

GLOBAL.EndailonCrisisLoreConcept.name: Endailon Crisis
GLOBAL.EndailonCrisisLoreConcept.description: Little is known about the Endailon Crisis, though it has become a topic of great interest among the scholars of Magehaven Lore. What has been established as commonly accepted knowledge, is that the Endailon Crisis happened in a distant age, before the first Godir set foot on Magehaven Lore. It was a conflict of cosmic scale, involving the Endailon Lore and possibly factions under their influence on one side, and the Archons Lore and their allies—notably among them the Ancient Krazura Lore—on the other. The Endailon Crisis ended with the Endailon Lore becoming locked within Grexolis Lore.

GLOBAL.EternalCouncilLoreConcept.name: Eternal Council
GLOBAL.EternalCouncilLoreConcept.description:
Originally, the Eternal Council was founded as a council of Giant King Lore, where the matters of Myrrida Lore and the many Worlds Within Lore which it spanned would be discussed under the honorary leadership of the Titans. Later, when the Traitor Kings Lore had revoked any allegiance to the Archons Lore, only the wisest of the Giant Kings remained in the Eternal Council. They moved the seat of the council away from Titan’s Henge and indeed their discussions focused less and less on the government of Myrrida Lore, but instead on the mysteries of the cosmos.

In scholarly union, the Eternal Council explored the various applications of crystal magic, seeking to employ Lithorite to immortalize their knowledge—and at last themselves. As their opus magnum, the Eternal Council transferred their souls into Lithorite crystals, escaping Archon judgment and becoming the Eternal Sages Lore.

GLOBAL.EternalSagesLoreConcept.name: Eternal Sages
GLOBAL.EternalSagesLoreConcept.description:
Once the wisest Giant Kings of Myrrida Lore, the Eternal Sages have left behind their mortal bodies, transferring their souls into Lithorite crystals. They are wielders of powerful crystal magic, commanding the Lithorine and blessing their followers with large stature and crystalline resilience.

The Eternal Sages no longer concern themselves much with the matters of mortals. Instead, all their actions are directed towards the collection and preservation of knowledge, which they store in vast crystal libraries of their own making. It is said that the Eternal Sages know the answer to every enigma the cosmos holds, yet persuading them to share any such knowledge can be a task for eternity.

GLOBAL.FireClanLoreConcept.name: Fire Clan
GLOBAL.FireClanLoreConcept.description: The most aggressive of the Giant Clans, the Fire Clan often seeks direct confrontation with the Rulers of a realm. Claiming distant heritage of Myrrida Lore, these Giants like to unleash terrible war beasts and wage war on the people settling in the lands they regard as their own.

GLOBAL.FractureLoreConcept.name: Fracture
GLOBAL.FractureLoreConcept.description:
Fractures are tears in the very fabric of magic, altering any spell cast near them. They were the byproduct of the Unmakers Lore' experiments and often appear around their ruins and magical wastes. Exposure to these fractures, or to the inward winds they produce, can mutate both mana and life itself.

Fractures grow unstable and increase in size as they swallow and twist magic, to a point where they can explode; scattering Astral Barrens, contaminating the area, and creating new fractures. A great number of unstable Fractures in a realm can cause a massive calamity, such as the cataclysm known as The Fracturing Lore.

GLOBAL.GeassadaeLoreConcept.name: Geassadae
GLOBAL.GeassadaeLoreConcept.description:
As the Duathadae Lore and their Mistwalker servants became a greater threat to the Godir Lore of Magehaven Lore, the general interest in the Fey realm Duatha Lore was rekindled, since old lore might expose the Duathadae's unknown weaknesses. The search through ancient scriptures and chronicles revealed that once a Circle Of Deogai Lore had existed on Duatha Lore, and—more importantly—that the Duathadae Lore may not be the only lords of the Fey.

Myths about the Geassadae were uncovered, powerful Fey who may have once ruled Duatha Lore, before falling victim to the Duathadae's dark enchantments. Though it has been warned that such tales may only be a perfidious variant of Fey trickery themselves.

GLOBAL.GiantsLoreConcept.name: Giants
GLOBAL.GiantsLoreConcept.description:
A relatively rare but imposing sight to behold, giants once roamed the primordial Worlds Within Lore in greater numbers. In the early days of the cosmos, giants directed the flow of the land and shaped the continents upon each world. This purportedly piqued the ire of the Dragons Lore who had formed worlds in a certain way before the giants and were unimpressed with their later adjustments.

True giants tend to come in various forms, usually associated with an element that they have a certain amount of control over. A number of offshoot races of Giantkin and other subtypes have also come into being over the ages through various intermingling of races.

GLOBAL.GiantKingLoreConcept.name: Giant King
GLOBAL.GiantKingLoreConcept.description: Sometimes Elder Giants, sometimes Giants of younger ages blessed with immense power and size, the Giant Kings trace their regal claim on the realms back to the Giant kingdom of Myrrida Lore. Masters of the forge and shapers of worlds, the Giant Kings are primal forces to be reckoned with. Gladly they will tell tales about the days of the Great Hunt, when Elder Giants tamed the Urwilderness Lore and slew its Primordial Beasts.

GLOBAL.GloomwatchLoreConcept.name: Gloomwatch
GLOBAL.GloomwatchLoreConcept.description: The Gloomwatch is a diverse faction, incorporating many different races and cultures. They are united by their worship of the Affinities Lore and the Dreamers Lore and their eternal fight against the forces of Urrath Lore. Their alleged history dates back to the Archons Lore and their first leader Irith of the Scrying Fountain, chronicling a mythic tale of how the Maer Lore and the Syron Lore descended from these celestial origins.

GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept.name: Godir
GLOBAL.GodirLoreConcept.description: The Wizards of the Pantheon Lore who gather at Magehaven Lore are called Godir. From there they seek new knowledge and journey to new realms in the Astral Sea. Some of the Godir are newly Ascended Champ Lore—while others are ancient Wizard King Lore or Elder Dragons, seeking dominion over new realms and people through their mastery of the Affinities Lore. Godir have achieved a form of immortality: if they are vanquished, they are cast into the Astral Void Lore and seek to rematerialize in Magehaven.

GLOBAL.GreatUmbralWarLoreConcept.name: Great Umbral War
GLOBAL.GreatUmbralWarLoreConcept.description:
The Great Umbral War broke out when Lithyl Lore launched an invasion on Athla Lore, unleashing the swarming hordes of Urrath Lore from the Shadow Realm Lore. Yet it was only the beginning, for soon thereafter Eldritch Sovereign Lore all across the Astral Sea Lore began similar assaults, enshrouding the Worlds Within Lore with their corruptive gloom.

Though the Godir Lore of Magehaven Lore attained the aid of the Gloomwatch Lore and later the Archons Lore, the enemy is tenacious and its maddening reach can corrupt even Godir. Therefore much hope is placed in the powers of the Endailon Lore, despite their unfathomable influence and motives.

GLOBAL.GrexolisLoreConcept.name: Grexolis
GLOBAL.GrexolisLoreConcept.description: A fractured World hidden in the mists of the Astral Sea Lore. The Archons Lore left a custodian to guard the secrets which lie buried here.

GLOBAL.HorwyndLoreConcept.name: Horwynd
GLOBAL.HorwyndLoreConcept.description:
When the Ancient Krazura Lore became locked in Grexolis Lore, their distant relatives, the Horwynd, took it upon themselves to preserve their knowledge and memory. They fled from the sphere of Archon influence and no chronicles speak of their destination or fate.

And yet they returned ages later, revealing the Shrouded Isles they created through unbreakable pacts with the Wizard King Lore. With pride they eulogize their Tree of Wisdom and its schools of magic. But their homeland and its history remain a mortal secret.

GLOBAL.LostWizardLoreConcept.name: Lost Wizard
GLOBAL.LostWizardLoreConcept.description:
A Lost Wizard was once a powerful wizard who, either by foolhardy choice or forced exile, found themselves in the Astral Void Lore and succumbed to the Shadow Trial Lore. These power-hungry husks now glide with deadly purpose through the Astral Sea Lore as one of the myriad Monsters that roam its depths, preying upon the unwary.

While it retains an affinity for magic and even clutches its Tome of Spells greedily, its physical form has twisted to match its environment.

GLOBAL.MaerLoreConcept.name: Maer
GLOBAL.MaerLoreConcept.description:
The Maer are a rare breed of sentient merfolk, residing deep within the Astral Sea Lore. Where mortals find travel through the Astral Sea tedious and dangerous, these beings move through it with ease and grace, singing along to songs no one else can hear.

The Maer are such a rare sight that many schooled mortals deem their existence a myth, a story of solace to explain the strange sounds heard during the travels through the Astral Sea. But these benevolent, solitary creatures of magic and song are as real as the horrors that plague the currents.

GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept.name: Magehaven
GLOBAL.MagehavenLoreConcept.description:
Magehaven is a World in the Astral Sea Lore where the Pantheon Lore of Godir Lore hold their most important forum of dispute and council. It is protected by an unbreakable spell which prevents any harm from being done to a living creature or Soul. Therefore, even the fiercest enemies can meet there to negotiate their conflicts.

Magehaven is located close to The Well Lore and bears remnants of the Archons Lore who once dwelt there. Among the many wonders of Magehaven are the Library of Ancient Tomes and the World Gate Lore, which act as magic portals through the Astral Sea.

GLOBAL.MagelocksLoreConcept.name: Magelock
GLOBAL.MagelocksLoreConcept.description:
Magelock weapons are magic-powered ranged weapons, derived from the ordnance created by mighty empires long since fallen. By fusing the arcane with the physical, Magelock mechanisms allow skilled marksmen to hit faraway targets with great impact and accuracy.

Magelock weaponry permeates all corners of the Astral Sea Lore, implying analogous origins on various realms, yet the remnants of the ruined Commonwealth Lore remain most infamous for wielding these terrible weapons.

GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept.name: Myrrida
GLOBAL.MyrridaLoreConcept.description:
Many myths surround the fabled kingdom of Myrrida, where Giant King Lore once ruled the small races across the Worlds Within Lore. Undeniable is the wealth and grandeur, still exhibited within its ruined monumental structures and cities. Yet there is much debate among Godir Lore about the fall of Myrrida. Some say the Giant King Lore became corrupted by their power, giving rise to the Traitor Kings Lore. Others blame Archon suppression for the destruction of a lost utopia.

Certain is that the Archons Lore and their allied Elder Dragons besieged Myrrida, ending the long Age of Giants and distantly presaging the Endailon Crisis Lore. While the various Giant Clans seek to carry on the legacy of their ancient forefathers, their deeds pale beside the marveled legends of Myrrida.

GLOBAL.ObbadothLoreConcept.name: Obbadoth
GLOBAL.ObbadothLoreConcept.description: Obbadoth is an infernal World ruled by Demonic Princes, where fiends make the laws and sins are virtuous. Many realms of this world are affected by spells which enhance one's primal urges, which often leads to bloodshed, debauchery, and everything in between. Very few Godir Lore can withstand Obbadoth's infernal influence.

GLOBAL.PantheonLoreConcept.name: Pantheon
GLOBAL.PantheonLoreConcept.description: With many Wizard Kings seeing themselves as living gods, it is no surprise their gathering at Magehaven Lore became known as the Pantheon. In this sanctuary the members of the Pantheon debate and scheme to alter the fate of the cosmos. The Pantheon consists of many factions and alliances, of which the Covenant Faction Lore and Shadrai Faction Lore are most prominent.

GLOBAL.PellariLoreConcept.name: Pellari
GLOBAL.PellariLoreConcept.description:
Not much is known about the Pellari, for reports from the Fey realm Duatha Lore are scarce and notoriously unreliable. What has been accepted as common knowledge is that the Pellari are a diverse group of different animalistic races which are united by their display of almost excessive friendliness and a preference for simple, pastoral life.

Some sources pick up on the theory that Duatha Lore is a Dreamer and propose that the Pellari are one of her childish creations; a proposition that often gets extended to the Fey themselves and their unique magic properties that seem to defy all arcane rules and reason.

GLOBAL.PrimalSpiritsLoreConcept.name: Primal Spirits
GLOBAL.PrimalSpiritsLoreConcept.description: Primal Spirits are spiritual representations of the many aspects of Nature, worshiped by various peoples in the Astral Sea Lore. Each Spirit brings its own doctrines on society, and followers look up to them for guidance throughout all aspects of life. There are many different beliefs surrounding these spirits, but they all have one thing in common: in battle their worshipers can call upon the powers of their chosen Spirit to empower and aid them. The most common Primal Spirits are the Sylvan Wolf, Ash Sabertooth, Mire Crocodile, Dune Serpent, Storm Crow, Glacial Mammoth, and Tunneling Spider.

GLOBAL.RevenantsLoreConcept.name: Revenants
GLOBAL.RevenantsLoreConcept.description: Once Archons Lore in life, the soul-cursed Revenants invoke the greatest fear in the enemies of Urrath Lore. For their unlife represents the ultimate triumph of corruption, when not even the most virtuous souls may escape. First encountered on Worlds locked through Seals, the Revenant curse has since then spread to many Necropolises which the Archons left behind in their cosmic wars.

GLOBAL.SchoolOfArtificingLoreConcept.name: School of Artificing
GLOBAL.SchoolOfArtificingLoreConcept.description: The disciples of the Horwynd Lore School of Artificing diligently collect and preserve magical artifacts and monuments. When the Scholars of Shrouding proposed to cache the Godir's secrets in the Shrouded Isle, the Scholars of Artificing drew on their expertise in magical structures to construct the Portals that connect these hidden Realms to the Worlds Within Lore.

GLOBAL.SchoolOfShroudingLoreConcept.name: School of Shrouding
GLOBAL.SchoolOfShroudingLoreConcept.description: The disciples of the Horwynd Lore School of Shrouding were conservators and archivists of secret knowledge found in the Worlds Within Lore. When the development of experimental spells was repressed by the Archons Lore, the guileful Scholars of Shrouding suggested securing them in the Shrouded Isle, while also shrouding the Portals that lead to them.

GLOBAL.SchoolOfVitalizingLoreConcept.name: School of Vitalizing
GLOBAL.SchoolOfVitalizingLoreConcept.description: The disciples of the Horwynd Lore School of Vitalizing were primarily conservators and breeders of flora and fauna. Once the Shrouded Isle were shaped, the Scholars of Vitalizing applied their knowledge of growth and life to create regenerating habitats, where the Godir's sanctuaries remain untouched by the oppression of the Archons Lore.

GLOBAL.SchoolOfWardingLoreConcept.name: School of Warding
GLOBAL.SchoolOfWardingLoreConcept.description: The disciples of the Horwynd Lore School of Warding were originally tasked with preserving knowledge of battle and war. When the Archons Lore established the Circle Of Deogai Lore, the School of honorable warriors and knights deployed their holy power to protect the Portals to the Shrouded Isle against invading forces and the inquisitive agents of the Archons.

GLOBAL.ShadowDemonsLoreConcept.name: Umbral Demons
GLOBAL.ShadowDemonsLoreConcept.description: The Umbral Demons, sometimes referred to as Shadow Demons, are molded by Urrath Lore. Their forbidden inception reputedly involves distorting corrupted souls into the shapes of the Umbral Demons. The tainted creatures feed on magic leaking from the Astral Sea Lore. They first consumed the world of their creation, until only the Shadow Realm Lore remained: A twisted husk filled with blackness and despair. Since then, the Umbral Demons have preyed on many worlds, including Athla Lore, allowing the Umbral Abyss to spread in their wake.

GLOBAL.ShadowRealmLoreConcept.name: Umbral Abyss
GLOBAL.ShadowRealmLoreConcept.description:
Beyond the Astral Sea Lore and even the Void an eldritch infestation lurks: The Umbral Abyss, the dominion of Urrath Lore. Here is where Shadow Demons Lore reign, molded through a vile corruption of the power of Creation itself. Vile and toxic to any living being, the Umbral Abyss ever seeks to corrupt the Astral Sea, tearing festering wounds into the Worlds Within Lore. The Archons Lore and the Gloomwatch Lore fight back against the corruption, but wherever they wage war, the scars of battle that stain the realms never fully heal.

Through the Ages, the Umbral Abyss has claimed many civilizations, and their remnants of knowledge and treasure have lured many adventurers and wizards to a fate many consider worse than death.

GLOBAL.ShadowTrialLoreConcept.name: Torment of Shadows
GLOBAL.ShadowTrialLoreConcept.description: In the darkness of the Astral Void Lore, the banished Wizards are tormented by visions and maddening voices. Survivors describe vastly different experiences, as if the cosmos creates a reckoning for a Wizard's individual actions and beliefs. Those that succumb are doomed to drift forever as a Lost Wizard Lore, mad husks of which little remains other than their lust for power.

GLOBAL.ShadraiFactionLoreConcept.name: Shad'rai
GLOBAL.ShadraiFactionLoreConcept.description: A group of ambitious Godir Lore who formed a volatile cabal in order to claim power within the Pantheon Lore and the Astral Sea Lore. They believe no power should be hidden from anyone and are known for their schemes and invasions of realms they deem worthy of their domination. Their chaotic tendencies often put them in direct opposition to the Covenant Faction Lore.

GLOBAL.SilverSeasLoreConcept.name: The Silver Seas
GLOBAL.SilverSeasLoreConcept.description:
The legend of the Silver Seas is anchored in the mind of every sailor. Ancient sea shanties tell of a place in the Worlds Within Lore where the Astral Currents converge, with seas so rich that their very waves are made of liquid silver. There, fish with scales of precious metals swim among reefs of pure mana, while the songs of the Maer Lore lull the shores.

Some seafarers theorize that the waves of the Silver Seas lie hidden within Tidolon Lore; others believe that their tides are yet to be found. Still, there are those who claim that this paradise is not a place to find, but a place to seek.

GLOBAL.SoulsLoreConcept.name: Souls
GLOBAL.SoulsLoreConcept.description:
Souls are the eternal Astral manifestations of all living beings. When someone dies, their soul is released to return to the Well of Creation. This journey through the Astral Flows Lore is arduous and many Astral Dwellers Lore hunt these souls. Especially troubled souls may find themselves lost or captured during the journey.

With specific magics, souls can be captured for nefarious purposes. Some dark races use souls as a valuable currency that allows the summoning of undead beings.

GLOBAL.StoneClanLoreConcept.name: Rock Clan
GLOBAL.StoneClanLoreConcept.description: Persistent and steady as stone, the Rock Clan has the patience to build what the other Giant Clans can only dream of conquering. They shun contact with the smaller races, going to great lengths to keep their dungeon halls, where faint echoes of Myrrida’s splendor are recalled, inaccessible.

GLOBAL.StormClanLoreConcept.name: Storm Clan
GLOBAL.StormClanLoreConcept.description: First silent then tempestuous, the Storm Clan prefers to strike when it is the least expected. The leaders of this Giant Clan study the lost magic of Myrrida Lore, seeking to emulate the arcane powers of the Giant King Lore of old.

GLOBAL.SyronLoreConcept.name: Syrons
GLOBAL.SyronLoreConcept.description: Originally descendants of the Maer Lore, the first Syrons were a part of the Gloomwatch Lore to protect the Dreamers Lore from the corrupting influence of Urrath Lore. They settled on idyllic worlds where the light of the Allfather Lore’s creation still burned bright, until the Shadow Demons Lore eventually invaded. Most of the Syrons were massacred and many of the survivors enslaved, their devoured home worlds overrun by the Shadow Realm Lore. The few Syrons that escaped spread across the Astral Sea, but many found themselves locked in an endless crusade against the Umbral Demons, even if they formally abandoned the Gloomwatch long ago.

GLOBAL.TheFracturingLoreConcept.name: the Fracturing
GLOBAL.TheFracturingLoreConcept.description:
The Fracturing was the magical cataclysm that erased the Unmakers Lore from the Worlds Within Lore and brought an end to their experiments. The few stories that survived the calamity speak of Fractures suddenly growing and erupting in a chain reaction.

Through the Fracturing, the affected worlds were changed forever. The land became barren, magic turned hazardous; some of their inhabitants adapted, and some were altered beyond recognition.

GLOBAL.TheWellLoreConcept.name: the Well
GLOBAL.TheWellLoreConcept.description: According to mythology, the Allfather Lore pulled the cosmos from the Well of Creation. All later creations of the Allfather Lore would date back to this one wonder. From Magehaven Lore, located deep in the Astral Sea Lore, the Well can be seen as a looming bright omen, a slowly swirling white maelstrom from which the light of creation emerges in shifting directions. All <Souls Lore>> of the dead are drawn to return to the Well on their final journey.

GLOBAL.TidolonLoreConcept.name: Tidolon
GLOBAL.TidolonLoreConcept.description: Tidolon is known for its vast oceans and relatively low density of land. Islands and small continents dot the massive sea of blue. Many aquatic beings thrive on this World, and it is said many lost treasures and whole empires are hidden beneath its surface.

GLOBAL.TomeLoreConcept.name: Tome
GLOBAL.TomeLoreConcept.description:
Tomes of power hold certain fundamental truths and secrets of the cosmos, often associated with specific Affinities Lore. These works are mystical manuscripts written by beings of power like Godir Lore, to pass on their mastery of the subject within.

True mastery of a Tome can only be achieved through dedicated focus. Every stage of mastery will grant powers that can alter realms and even a Godir's subjects themselves.

GLOBAL.TraitorKingsLoreConcept.name: Traitor Kings
GLOBAL.TraitorKingsLoreConcept.description:
The Traitor Kings were the Giant King Lore of old Myrrida Lore who broke allegiance to the Titans, ending the ancient agreement between Elder Giants and Archons Lore. Drunk on the glory of their kingdom they rejected a faith centered on the Allfather Lore, proclaiming that the Giant King Lore themselves had acted as gods and should therefore be worshiped as such.

Acting as ruthless overlords the Traitor Kings engaged in dark magic, twisting stolen knowledge from the Eternal Council Lore to achieve immortality. Yet when the war with the Archons Lore and Elder Dragons reached their thrones, they fell one by one, leaving only myths of their corrupt souls still haunting the ruins of Myrrida Lore.

GLOBAL.UnmakersLoreConcept.name: Unmakers
GLOBAL.UnmakersLoreConcept.description:
The Unmakers were a group of ambitious wizards whose experiments devastated large sections of the Astral Sea Lore, now known as the Fractured Realms. They rose to power after the Endailon Crisis Lore had destroyed or weakened the dominant forces of previous ages. Believing themselves capable of unraveling the very essence of mana and magic, the Unmakers competed and cooperated among themselves, striving to recreate the powers flowing from the Well of Creation.

Among the nomadic tribes of the Fractured Worlds, countless cautionary tales speak of the Unmakers and their experiments: how they tore the fabrics of magic, scarred the realms with Fractures — and ultimately, as the moral of the story, perished in the The Fracturing Lore that reshaped the realms.

GLOBAL.UrrathLoreConcept.name: Urrath
GLOBAL.UrrathLoreConcept.description: Urrath is the nemesis of the Archons Lore and widely believed to be the bringer of darkness and corruption to the cosmos. The most terrifying creatures known to exist, such as the Astral Monsters Lore, are blamed on Urrath's influence, as is all evil running through the veins of mortal races.

GLOBAL.UrwildernessLoreConcept.name: Urwilderness
GLOBAL.UrwildernessLoreConcept.description:
When the Elder Dragons shaped the Worlds Within Lore, they aroused the great beasts dwelling in its raw primal shell. Calling upon the powers of the Nature Endailon, these Primordial Beasts surrounded themselves in an overgrown Urwilderness, where creatures of many vicious, but also graceful, designs came to be and that even the Elder Dragons and Giants shunned.

Thus, when the small races arrived on the realms, their spreading settlements soon clashed with the enduring jungle of the Urwilderness. Enraged by the intrusions of civilization, the Primordial Beasts started to rampage across the realms, destroying everything in their wake.

Moved by the woes of the small races, the Elder Giants rose to their defense, initiating the Great Hunt. Gifted with the celestial chains of the Archons Lore, the Elder Giants thinned out the Urwilderness and bound the Primordial Beasts within mighty prisons. It was the dawn of the Age of Giants and thereupon the founding of Myrrida Lore.

GLOBAL.ValleyofWondersLoreConcept.name: Valley of Wonders
GLOBAL.ValleyofWondersLoreConcept.description: The Valley of Wonders is a historic area on the Blessed Continent on the world of Athla Lore. Once the home of the Elven Court of House Inioch, it has seen much turmoil since the first Athlan humans sacked the fabled court. It remains an area of great natural beauty and magical potency.

GLOBAL.WizardKingLoreConcept.name: Wizard King
GLOBAL.WizardKingLoreConcept.description: Wizard Kings are ancient archmages who seek power across the realms of the Astral Sea Lore. Before joining the Pantheon Lore at Magehaven Lore, the Shadow Trial Lore left many mentally warped. Wizard Kings are no longer limited to their original mortal form, and can create people vastly different from themselves.

GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept.name: Worlds Within
GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept.description:
The material worlds embedded within the Astral Sea Lore. They are the places where mortal races thrive and build their empires, and where the grand plots of the past and coming ages unfold.

According to ancient knowledge, the worlds were drawn from the The Well Lore by the Allfather Lore, after which Dragons Lore shaped them and Giants Lore refined them. Through the ages, the worlds and their distinguished realms have been altered and reshaped by various factions and forces, making each uniquely distinct in terms of the lay of the land, creatures and people living there, but also the abundance of magic and its representing Affinities Lore.

GLOBAL.WorldGateLoreConcept.name: World Gate
GLOBAL.WorldGateLoreConcept.description: To shortcut the dangerous journey to other Worlds, the Godir Lore have devised elaborate portal structures known as World Gates, which allow the user to travel to other worlds almost instantly. Great knowledge and skill is required to use such a portal. Otherwise, the Godir and their companions may be lost in the Astral Void Lore or stranded on an isolated world.

GLOBAL.SpellConcept.name: Spell
GLOBAL.SpellConcept.description:
Magical rites and incantations used by Leader. Obtained through Research.

Spells usually cost Mana and World Map Casting Point or Combat Casting Point.

Spells are divided in 2 main categories, depending on where they can be cast. Each category has their own collection of spell types:World Map SpellCombat Spell

GLOBAL.ClassicTurnConcept.name: Classic Turn
GLOBAL.ClassicTurnConcept.description: Player take Turn one after the other.

GLOBAL.SimultaneousTurnConcept.name: Simultaneous Turn
GLOBAL.SimultaneousTurnConcept.description: Player act simultaneously until they all end their Turn.

GLOBAL.ClaimConcept.name: Claim
GLOBAL.ClaimConcept.description:
Province Claims indicate the intention of owning a Province.

They appear on Province adjacent to:A City DomainOutpostExplored Ancient Wonder

If other Leader build on claimed provinces, the Rulers will meet and have a Casus Belli against them. Building on a province claimed by a Independent City will incur a Independent City Relation penalty.

Rulers also have distant claims on provinces up to a distance of 3 away from their owned domain. Distant claims yield less severe penalties and are only violated by building an outpost or exploring an Ancient Wonder.

GLOBAL.StructureProductionConcept.name: Production
GLOBAL.StructureProductionConcept.description:
Production is used for building City Structure.

Every Turn, Production is spent on the first structure in the City's Production Queue. Leftover Production becomes Surplus.

Gain Production by: Annexing Iron Deposits.Building Foresters and Quarries in Province.Building certain City Structure.Collecting Pickup.

GLOBAL.FoodConcept.name: Food
GLOBAL.FoodConcept.description: Used in cities to gain new Population.

GLOBAL.ProductionConcept.name: Production
GLOBAL.ProductionConcept.description:
Production is used in City as the base value for both Unit Production and Structure Production, enabling cities to produce items faster.

Gain Production by: Annexing Iron Deposits.Building Foresters and Quarries in Province.

GLOBAL.RecruitmentPointsConcept.name: Recruitment Point
GLOBAL.RecruitmentPointsConcept.description: Recruitment points are used in the Request Military Aid to draft Unit into your Empire or to send them to aid in the defense of vassal houses. Recruitment points are primarily gained from Independent City Relation with Independent City.

GLOBAL.UnitProductionConcept.name: Draft
GLOBAL.UnitProductionConcept.description:
Draft is used for recruiting Unit in City.

Spent on the first Unit in the City's Unit Production Queue every Turn. Leftover Draft becomes Surplus.

Gain Draft by:Building certain City Structure.

GLOBAL.BindingEssenceConcept.name: Binding Essence
GLOBAL.BindingEssenceConcept.description:
Binding Essence and Fragments are the remains of magical items.

They are used for crafting custom items in the Item Forge.
Crafting Tier 3 or 4 items costs Binding Fragments in addition to the Binding Essence cost.

Binding Essence is gained by disenchanting any items in the arsenal.
Binding Fragments are gained by disenchanting Tier 3 or 4 items in the arsenal.

GLOBAL.DiplomaticTokenConcept.name: Whispering Stone
GLOBAL.DiplomaticTokenConcept.description:
Whispering Stones are given to a Independent City to begin Negotiation, which can lead to it becoming your Vassal. Having more allows you to befriend multiple Independent City at once.

Unused Whispering Stones can be given to your City to gain City Stability.

Gain more Whispering Stones via Empire Development

GLOBAL.GoldConcept.name: Gold
GLOBAL.GoldConcept.description:
Gold is your material wealth and riches. Used for:Recruiting new Unit.Paying Unit Upkeep.Building City Structure.

Gain Gold by: Annexing Gold Veins.Building Mines in Province.Building certain City Structure.Collecting Pickup.

GLOBAL.ImperiumConcept.name: Imperium
GLOBAL.ImperiumConcept.description:
Imperium represents your authority and reputation in the mortal realm.

Used for:Founding City from Outpost.Taking over conquered City.Buying Empire Skills.
Gain Imperium by developing the Wizard Tower in your Throne City and by annexing Ancient Wonder.

GLOBAL.InfluenceConcept.name: Whispering Stone Strength
GLOBAL.InfluenceConcept.description: Whispering Stones have a certain strength that determines how effective they are at manipulating Free Cities. During Negotiations, Whispering Stones generate allegiance based on their strength. The higher the strength, the sooner the Negotiations will succeed.

GLOBAL.KnowledgeConcept.name: Knowledge
GLOBAL.KnowledgeConcept.description:
Knowledge is the collective arcane wisdom of your sages and wise men, as they explore the secrets of the magical Affinity.

Used for researching Spell and other skills from Tome.
Unlocking a tome increases the knowledge cost of all skills in future tomes.

If there is no active research, then leftover Knowledge will be kept as Surplus.

Gain Knowledge by:Building Research Posts in Province.Building certain City Structure.Collecting Pickup.

GLOBAL.ManaConcept.name: Mana
GLOBAL.ManaConcept.description:
Mana is the raw source of magic. Used for:Casting Spell.Summoning magical Unit.Paying Unit Upkeep.
Gain Mana by: Annexing Mana Nodes.Building Conduits in Province.Building certain City Structure.Collecting Pickup.

GLOBAL.AncientWonderConcept.name: Ancient Wonder
GLOBAL.AncientWonderConcept.description:
An Ancient Wonder is a Location that contains adventure and rewards. It can only be explored by a single Army led by a Hero.

When cleared, it can be annexed by a City. When annexed it will provide City Income and special Unit in the Request Military Aid. An annexed Ancient Wonder counts as a type of Province Improvement.

Ancient Wonders can be Bronze, Silver, or Gold, depending on rarity, difficulty and value.

GLOBAL.CityCenterConcept.name: City Center
GLOBAL.CityCenterConcept.description: The Location on the World Map which lies at the origin of the City Domain.

GLOBAL.CityTierConcept.name: City Tier
GLOBAL.CityTierConcept.description: City Tier is determined by its last completed Town Hall City Structure.

GLOBAL.ConduitConcept.name: Conduit
GLOBAL.ConduitConcept.description: A Conduit is a base Province Improvement with the following benefits:Provides Mana income.

GLOBAL.DomainConcept.name: Domain
GLOBAL.DomainConcept.description: The collection of Province belonging to the city. The Ruler will have a Claim on provinces adjacent to their city domain. Friendly units have to spend {amount1} less Move Point to traverse terrain in friendly domains.

GLOBAL.FarmConcept.name: Farm
GLOBAL.FarmConcept.description: A Farm is a base Province Improvement with the following benefits:Provides Food income.

GLOBAL.FisheryConcept.name: Fishery
GLOBAL.FisheryConcept.description: A Fishery is a base Province Improvement with the following benefits:Provides Food income.

GLOBAL.ForeignCityConcept.name: Foreign City
GLOBAL.ForeignCityConcept.description: City belonging to an Empire other than your own.

GLOBAL.ForesterConcept.name: Forester
GLOBAL.ForesterConcept.description: A Forester is a base Province Improvement with the following benefits:Provides Food and Structure Production income.

GLOBAL.GuildSlotConcept.name: Guild Slot
GLOBAL.GuildSlotConcept.description:
Represents a City's capacity for powerful economic City Structure called Guilds.

Typically a city will only have a single Guild Slot.

GLOBAL.InfestationConcept.name: Infestation
GLOBAL.InfestationConcept.description:
Areas under the control of Marauder, who increase in numbers and over time take over adjacent Province. They will periodically send forth raiding parties that can potentially start a Siege on a City without needing a Hero.

Destroying the Infestation Spawner will clear the infestation and grant the destroyer great rewards based on tier and size of the Infestation.

When an Infestation grows into one of your Province, it will continuously pillage its Province Improvement until the Infestation Spawner is destroyed.

Infestations have several states, its Infestation Spawner will indicate its current state, and each state will take several Turn to activate: Deep Sleep/Sleeping/Awakening. The infestation will become active. Patrolling. The infestation will patrol its domain. Invasion. A raiding party will emerge. Recovering. The infestation will reinforce its patrolling armies.
Infestations can be Infestation Neutrality to certain Empire.

GLOBAL.InfestationNeutralityConcept.name: Neutral
GLOBAL.InfestationNeutralityConcept.description:
Infestation are hostile to all Empire by default, but they can become neutral to one or more Empires in certain circumstances.

While neutral to an Empire:The Infestation's armies will never attack the Empire.The Infestation will not pillage the Empire's Province Improvements.The Infestation will not send out raiding parties to the Empire.The Infestation can still grow into the Empire's domain.If the Empire attacks the Infestation's armies, the Infestation stops being neutral towards the Empire.
Infestations summoned by an Empire always start out neutral towards them.

GLOBAL.InfestationSpawnerConcept.name: Infestation Spawner
GLOBAL.InfestationSpawnerConcept.description: An Infestation Spawner is a Location that causes an Infestation to take place.

GLOBAL.LocationConcept.name: Location
GLOBAL.LocationConcept.description:
A special building or site on the World Map, such as a watchtower, gold vein or bandit lair.
Guarded locations can be conquered to earn rewards.Take ownership of a location by moving Unit onto to it.Many locations give Resource when within a city's domain.

GLOBAL.MagicMaterialConcept.name: Magic Material
GLOBAL.MagicMaterialConcept.description:
Magic Materials are Node that provide bonus effects to your Empire, as well as provide City Income. These bonus effects can be traded to other Empire and Independent City.

If all Magic Materials of the type are collected, they will provide an additional powerful bonus. The following bonuses are available:

T O K E N S E T B O N U S. I M P E R I A L_ E S S E N C ET O K E N S E T B O N U S. C O S M I C F L U X_ E L I X I RT O K E N S E T B O N U S. R I N G S_ O F_ B I N D I N G

GLOBAL.MineConcept.name: Mine
GLOBAL.MineConcept.description: A Mine is a base Province Improvement with the following benefits:Provides Gold income.

GLOBAL.NodeConcept.name: Resource Node
GLOBAL.NodeConcept.description: Nodes are Location on the World Map which grant bonus income when the Province they are located in is annexed to a City.

GLOBAL.PickupConcept.name: Pickup
GLOBAL.PickupConcept.description:
One-time Resource packs on the World Map. Their rewards can be acquired by moving an Army onto them.

A Pickup is removed once its rewards are collected.

GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept.name: Province Improvement
GLOBAL.ProvinceImprovementConcept.description:
Structures that a City builds in a Province to add that province to its Domain.

Different improvements are available in a province depending on what Province Feature and Location are within it.

A city can support one improvement for each Population it has after the first one.

GLOBAL.QuarryConcept.name: Quarry
GLOBAL.QuarryConcept.description: A Quarry is a base Province Improvement with the following benefits:Provides Structure Production income.

GLOBAL.ResearchPostConcept.name: Research Post
GLOBAL.ResearchPostConcept.description: A Research Post is a base Province Improvement with the following benefits:Provides Knowledge income.

GLOBAL.RootNodeConcept.name: Root Node
GLOBAL.RootNodeConcept.description: Node required to achieve Magic Victory. Base Root Nodes provide Mana and can be converted to a different Affinity for additional City Income.

GLOBAL.RuinedNodeConcept.name: Ruined Node
GLOBAL.RuinedNodeConcept.description: Ruined Nodes are Node that have been depleted by overharvesting or other means.Ruined Nodes no longer provide any income or bonuses.Ruined Nodes still grant the option of building certain Province Improvement in the Province their intact versions would allow.Ruined Nodes can be restored as long as you have claimed them, restoring them costs Mana.This cost is decreased each Turn the Ruined Node exists, until a minimum cost is reached.When restored, Ruined Nodes are replaced by their intact versions which provide their income and bonuses again.

GLOBAL.WizardTowerConcept.name: Wizard Tower
GLOBAL.WizardTowerConcept.description:
The Wizard Tower is the center of a Leader's powers. Only one can be built in the Throne City after building the Town Hall II .

It unlocks Empire-wide benefits, provides Imperium income, and improves the Vision Range of the Throne City.

Allows the construction of the Item Forge after building the S T R U C T U R E_ U P G R A D E S. W I Z A R D_ T O W E R_ F O U N D A T I O N.

GLOBAL.AbsorbingConcept.name: Absorbing
GLOBAL.AbsorbingConcept.description: Absorbing a City makes it part of your Empire under your direct control, retaining its original race and culture.

GLOBAL.AdvisorConcept.name: Advisor
GLOBAL.AdvisorConcept.description:
The Advisor shows new tutorial and advice messages. Advice messages contain tips about the current situation of your empire.

It can be accessed through the ? banner located near the bottom right of the screen.

GLOBAL.AffinityConcept.name: Affinity
GLOBAL.AffinityConcept.description:
The Affinity of an Empire is an indication of its strengths, specializations, and available Tome.

The Affinity types are:OrderChaosNatureMateriumAstralShadow

Starting Affinity points are determined by faction creation choices. Affinity points are obtained by selecting the respective Tome during Research.

Having more Affinity points will increase the rate at which you unlock new Empire Skill in Empire Development.

To unlock higher tier Tome, you will need to have a certain amount of Affinity points that match with the Affinity of those tomes.

GLOBAL.ArmyConcept.name: Army
GLOBAL.ArmyConcept.description:
An army is a collection of maximum 6 Unit.

Armies can be moved on the World Map, explore Location, collect Pickup, and engage in Combat.

GLOBAL.ArtifactConcept.name: Artifact
GLOBAL.ArtifactConcept.description:
Artifacts are unique items bound to the Empire of a Player. They provide unique bonuses to the Empire controlling them.
Artifacts are often part of a collection. Completing the collection will trigger an impactful Collection Happening.Artifacts may be traded between Player.When defeating a player, all Artifacts of that player are claimed by the defeating player.

GLOBAL.AstralEchoesConcept.name: Astral Echoes
GLOBAL.AstralEchoesConcept.description: Mysterious whispers of the Astral Sea, only visible to and collectible by Mystics.

GLOBAL.BoostConcept.name: Boost
GLOBAL.BoostConcept.description:
Boosting a City Structure reduces its cost by {costreduction}.

Boosts automatically apply when the requirements are met.

GLOBAL.BuffDebuffSpellConcept.name: Buff/Debuff Spell
GLOBAL.BuffDebuffSpellConcept.description: Buffs allies and debuffs enemies in battle.Costs Mana and Combat Casting Point.

GLOBAL.HealingBuffSpellConcept.name: Healing/Buff Spell
GLOBAL.HealingBuffSpellConcept.description: Heals and buffs allies in battle.Costs Mana and Combat Casting Point.

GLOBAL.BuffSpellConcept.name: Buff Spell
GLOBAL.BuffSpellConcept.description: Buffs allies in battle.Costs Mana and Combat Casting Point.

GLOBAL.CapturedConcept.name: Captured
GLOBAL.CapturedConcept.description: Captured units may be recruited after combat by spending War Spoils or Gold for non-Reaver empires.

GLOBAL.CastingLimitConcept.name: Casting Limit
GLOBAL.CastingLimitConcept.description: Casting Limit controls how many World Map Spell the user can cast in a single turn on the World Map. Casting Limit can be increased by building the S T R U C T U R E_ U P G R A D E S. C H A N N E L I N G C H A M B E R in your Throne City.

GLOBAL.CityBattlementStructureConcept.name: Battlement Structure
GLOBAL.CityBattlementStructureConcept.description:
Battlement Structures are a type of City Defense Structure which spawns Battlement obstacles directly behind the walls in Combat during a Siege.

Battlement obstacles provide buffs for units standing inside them.

When multiple Battlement Structures are built, only the most powerful Battlement obstacles will be present in Combat.

GLOBAL.CityCapConcept.name: City Cap
GLOBAL.CityCapConcept.description:
The number of City your Empire can control.

Exceeding your City Cap results in {incomepercentage} City Income to all your City for each City above City Cap.

Your City Cap can be increased through Empire Development

GLOBAL.CityDefenseStructureConcept.name: City Defense Structure
GLOBAL.CityDefenseStructureConcept.description:
City Defense Structures are City Structure that typically grant Fortification Health and provide defensive benefits in Combat during a Siege.

There are different types of Defense Structures:City Wall StructureCity Tower StructureCity Support StructureCity Battlement Structure

GLOBAL.CityConcept.name: City
GLOBAL.CityConcept.description:
Cities are located on the World Map. Cities are built by upgrading an Outpost or conquered through War.

A city may either belong to an Empire or be aIndependent City.

The Domain of a city expands according to its Population. Cities provide City Income, which can be improved by adding City Structure and Province Improvement.

GLOBAL.CityIncomeConcept.name: City Income
GLOBAL.CityIncomeConcept.description: City Income is the amount of Resource a City generates each Turn.

GLOBAL.CityRuinConcept.name: City Ruin
GLOBAL.CityRuinConcept.description: Remnants of a City. Can be rebuilt into a city for a cost.

GLOBAL.CitySpellConcept.name: City Spell
GLOBAL.CitySpellConcept.description: Can affect the targeted city and its domain.Costs Mana and World Map Casting Point.

GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept.name: City Structure
GLOBAL.CityStructureConcept.description:
City Structures provide economic bonuses for the City they are built in.

They usually cost Structure Production and Gold, and are built using the Structure Queue.

GLOBAL.CitySupportStructureConcept.name: Support Structure
GLOBAL.CitySupportStructureConcept.description:
Support Structures are a type of City Defense Structure which adds Combat Enchantment to the Combat in a Siege.

These Combat Enchantment add tactical benefits to the Defender in Combat.

Multiple Support Structures can be built and active in one City.

GLOBAL.CityTowerStructureConcept.name: Tower Structure
GLOBAL.CityTowerStructureConcept.description:
Tower Structures are a type of City Defense Structure which spawns Tower units in Combat during a Siege.
Tower units are typically long range units that cannot move and act automatically.

When multiple Tower Structures are built, only the most powerful Tower units will be present in Combat.

GLOBAL.CityWallStructureConcept.name: Wall Structure
GLOBAL.CityWallStructureConcept.description:
Wall Structures are a type of City Defense Structure which adds the requirement to Siege the City before hostile armies can attack.

They also define the Wall obstacles present in Combat during a Siege.

When multiple Wall Structures are present, only the strongest Wall obstacle is present in combat.

GLOBAL.CombatEnchantmentConcept.name: Combat Enchantment
GLOBAL.CombatEnchantmentConcept.description:
A type of Spell that affects the entire battlefield.

While active, the spell triggers an effect at the start of the caster's Turn.

GLOBAL.CombatSpellConcept.name: Combat Spell
GLOBAL.CombatSpellConcept.description:
These are Spell that are cast during Combat, using Combat Casting Point.

Types of Combat Spells are:Buff SpellCombat EnchantmentCombat Summon SpellDamage SpellDebuff SpellHealing Spell

GLOBAL.CombatSummonSpellConcept.name: Combat Summon Spell
GLOBAL.CombatSummonSpellConcept.description:
A type of Spell that summons a Unit with P R O P E R T I E S. M A G I C_ O R I G I N onto any hex during Combat.

Units summoned in this way die when combat ends.

GLOBAL.EmpireDevelopmentConcept.name: Empire Development
GLOBAL.EmpireDevelopmentConcept.description:
Contains Empire Skill that can improve your empire's economy and unlock important abilities such as Seafaring and Tunneling.

Empire Skill become available when enough Affinity Progress has been attained towards that particular Affinity. Available Empire Skill can be unlocked at any time by paying their Imperium cost.

GLOBAL.EmpireSkillConcept.name: Empire Skill
GLOBAL.EmpireSkillConcept.description:
Unlocks Empire-wide bonuses or grants powerful one-off rewards. Acquired via Empire Development.

Empire Skills require certain levels of Affinity to unlock.

GLOBAL.ItemTransportationConcept.name: Item Transportation
GLOBAL.ItemTransportationConcept.description:
An item goes into transportation when you unequip it. When an item is being transported, it is unavailable for all heroes.

While in transport the item: Doesn't count towards arsenal effects.Can not be disenchanted.Can not be equipped.Can not be traded with other rulers.

GLOBAL.SpeedMarchConcept.name: Forced March
GLOBAL.SpeedMarchConcept.description:
Forced March can be used to force your units to move further on the World Map than they would normally be able to in a single Turn.

When Forced March is activated units gain {Movepointgain}% of their Move Point but lose {Healthloss}% of their current Hit Point. They also become P R O P E R T I E S. E X H A U S T E D for {ExhaustedTurns} Turn. Forced March costs {Manacost} Mana per unit in the army.

The ability to use Forced March can be unlocked through Empire Development .

GLOBAL.TradeRouteConcept.name: Trade Route
GLOBAL.TradeRouteConcept.description:
A connection between a City and an Outpost or other City, granting the origin city where it was created income based on the target it is connected to.

Cities can establish a Trade Route by spending Unit Production, the cost increasing with the type of target and the amount of movement needed to reach it.

Only a certain number of Trade Routes can be active per City, this cap can be increased via City Structure.

GLOBAL.CryptConcept.name: Crypt
GLOBAL.CryptConcept.description:
When you defeat an enemy Hero in combat, they have a chance to go to your Prison or your crypt.

The remains of these heroes can be sold to get their equipment and some gold.

GLOBAL.DamageDebuffSpellConcept.name: Damage/Debuff Spell
GLOBAL.DamageDebuffSpellConcept.description: Damages and debuffs enemies in battle.Costs Mana and Combat Casting Point.

GLOBAL.DamageHealingSpellConcept.name: Damage/Healing Spell
GLOBAL.DamageHealingSpellConcept.description: Damages enemies and heals allies in battle.Costs Mana and Combat Casting Point.

GLOBAL.DamageSpellConcept.name: Damage Spell
GLOBAL.DamageSpellConcept.description: Damages enemies in battle.Costs Mana and Combat Casting Point.

GLOBAL.DebuffSpellConcept.name: Debuff Spell
GLOBAL.DebuffSpellConcept.description: Debuffs enemies in battle.Costs Mana and Combat Casting Point.

GLOBAL.DormantConcept.name: Dormant
GLOBAL.DormantConcept.description: Dormant skills do not grant any gameplay effects and cannot be reset.

GLOBAL.EmpireBonusConcept.name: Empire Bonus
GLOBAL.EmpireBonusConcept.description: Empire bonuses provide passive effects, new options or new mechanics. Once researched, they are immediately active and do not require a spell to be cast.

GLOBAL.EmpireConcept.name: Empire
GLOBAL.EmpireConcept.description:
An empire consists of a Leader, their Army, City and Domain.

An empire that has lost both its Leader and Throne City is defeated.

GLOBAL.EnemyArmySpellConcept.name: Enemy Army Spell
GLOBAL.EnemyArmySpellConcept.description: Affects an enemy army.Costs Mana and World Map Casting Point.

GLOBAL.EquipmentConcept.name: Equipment
GLOBAL.EquipmentConcept.description:
Equipment is items such as weapons and armor that Leader and Hero can equip to gain bonuses and abilities in Combat or in the World Map.

Equipment can typically be gained from Pickup, Ancient Wonder, and Quests.

Equipment that is not equipped is shared between the Ruler and all Heroes of the same Empire.

Rulers and Heroes have a number of equipment slots where 1 equipment item can be assigned of the corresponding type.

Types of equipment slots are:Primary Secondary Head Torso Legs Mount Ring Miscellaneous

GLOBAL.ExcavationConcept.name: Excavation
GLOBAL.ExcavationConcept.description:
Excavation is a World Map ability available to Unit which allows them to dig through tunnels and clear out Province in the Underground that lies underneath Earthen terrain.

Excavation can open up new paths, uncover buried Treasure, or even discover hidden Location.

GLOBAL.FeudalHouseConcept.name: Feudal House
GLOBAL.FeudalHouseConcept.description:
Cities belonging to players of the Feudal Aristocracy subculture gain an associated House.
The Governor becomes the P R O P E R T I E S. L I E G E_ L O R D of that city's House.Units produced in that City gain that City's House, gaining reduced upkeep and increased health regeneration while in their P R O P E R T I E S. L I E G E_ L O R D's army.Units belonging to the house additionally gain a powerful boost in combat while in the army of their P R O P E R T I E S. L I E G E_ L O R D.These benefits increase based on the P R O P E R T I E S. L I E G E_ L O R D's Renown Level.In addition, when the P R O P E R T I E S. L I E G E_ L O R D gains Renown, the units belonging to their house gain a small amount of Experience.

Units summoned on the Strategic Map or gained through events join the house of the most powerful nearby friendly army.
Units recruited through Rally of the Lieges gain the House of the City they're recruited to.

When a Governor is first assigned to a City, you may choose the House's name and banner.
This can be edited at any time in the same manner one changes the city's name, by clicking the name in the city panel.

GLOBAL.FeudalLordConcept.name: Feudal Lord
GLOBAL.FeudalLordConcept.description: The Feudal Culture can grant {herocount} Hero special Feudal Lord titles as Hero Skills. They grant bonuses to the City these Hero are governor of or World Map bonuses to their Army. The Hero Skills are:S K I L L S. F E U D A L_ L O R D_ W A RS K I L L S. F E U D A L_ L O R D_ C R O P SS K I L L S. F E U D A L_ L O R D_ K N O W L E D G ES K I L L S. F E U D A L_ L O R D_ M A G I CS K I L L S. F E U D A L_ L O R D_ P R O D U C T I O N

GLOBAL.FogOfWarConcept.name: Fog of War
GLOBAL.FogOfWarConcept.description:
Hexes on the World Map that have been previously revealed but you currently have no vision of through Army or Location owned by you are covered by Fog of War.

Hexes within Fog of War appear darker than when revealed by vision, but will still reveal terrain types, roads and Location. Neutral and Hostile Army are not visible within Fog of War unless sensed by Sensor Range.

Through Treaty and Pv E Dipl State you may reveal other City. But they will still be covered by Fog of War.

GLOBAL.FoundingConcept.name: Founding
GLOBAL.FoundingConcept.description:
Outpost can be transformed into City by spending Imperium.

Pay attention to your City Cap when founding new cities, you will suffer economic penalties if you have too many cities!

GLOBAL.FriendlyArmySpellConcept.name: Friendly Army Spell
GLOBAL.FriendlyArmySpellConcept.description: Affects a friendly army.Costs Mana and World Map Casting Point.

GLOBAL.GovernorConcept.name: Governor
GLOBAL.GovernorConcept.description:
A Governor is a Leader or Hero assigned to govern a City.

Each hero has a Governance Trait that determines the bonuses they give to their city. These bonuses can be increased with Renown earned from fulfilling the hero's Ambition.

A Ruler is always the Governor of their Throne City.

GLOBAL.HandcraftedRegionConcept.name: Handcrafted Region
GLOBAL.HandcraftedRegionConcept.description:
Handcrafted Regions are a collection of Province that are custom made rather than fully randomly generated. They generally contain the same type of Location as normal Provinces but can contain special visuals, shapes or an unique combination of Province Feature.

Certain Realm Traits, such as Legends of Myrrida can add additional Handcrafted Regions that would otherwise never be added to a realm.

GLOBAL.HealingSpellConcept.name: Healing Spell
GLOBAL.HealingSpellConcept.description: Heals allies in battle.Costs Mana and Combat Casting Point.

GLOBAL.HeroCapConcept.name: Hero Cap
GLOBAL.HeroCapConcept.description:
The hero cap represents the number of Hero your Empire can support.

You cannot recruit more heroes beyond the cap. The cap will increase automatically as the game goes on. You can spend Imperium to increase it instantly.

GLOBAL.HyperlinkConcept.name: Hyperlink
GLOBAL.HyperlinkConcept.description: As you can see, this tooltip opened as you hovered over the hyperlink. Now try hovering over this Hyperlink to open a tooltip within the tooltip!

GLOBAL.InfusionConcept.name: Infusion
GLOBAL.InfusionConcept.description:
Infusions are individual improvements that can be put on created items in the Item Forge. These can be Passive Properties, Active Abilities or Damage Channels.

An Infusion has an Infusion Point cost, which increases the cost to forge that item.

Each Infusion after the first also increases the total price of forging the item by {amount1}%.

GLOBAL.InfusionPointConcept.name: Infusion Point
GLOBAL.InfusionPointConcept.description:
Every Infusion has a specific Infusion Point cost ranging from {amount1} to {amount2}. Normally an item can have no more than {amount3} Infusion Points.

The Infusion Point total determines the Item Tier as follows:Item Tier I: 1 or 2 Infusion PointsItem Tier II: 3 Infusion PointsItem Tier III: 4 Infusion PointsItem Tier IV: 5+ Infusion Points

GLOBAL.ItemForgeConcept.name: Item Forge
GLOBAL.ItemForgeConcept.description:
The Item Forge is used to create new custom hero items. Forging items costs Binding Essence, Gold, and time. Only a single item can be forged at a time.

The cost and time to forge an item depend on the amount of Infusion Point used to forge the item. The amount of Infusion also increases the cost.

The Infusions available are dependent on the types of Magic Material that you have collected. Collecting more of the same Magic Material will unlock more powerful Infusions.

The Item Forge can be build in your Wizard Tower.

GLOBAL.ItemTierConcept.name: Item Tier
GLOBAL.ItemTierConcept.description:
An item's tier is an indication of its power. The damage of Primary Weapons increases with each tier based on what type of weapon it is.

In the Item Forge, the item tier is determined by the amount of Infusion.

GLOBAL.EldritchRelicWeaponConcept.name: Eldritch Relic Weapon
GLOBAL.EldritchRelicWeaponConcept.description:
These are powerful weapons exclusive to Eldritch Sovereign Lore. They grant two attacks, one long range and one melee range.

Usable by:Hero Class RitualistHero Class Mage

GLOBAL.FistWeaponConcept.name: Fist Weapon
GLOBAL.FistWeaponConcept.description:
These are small weapons that are used in each hand. They grant the hero melee attacks that often have a special effect on the third attack.

Usable by:Hero Class DefenderHero Class WarriorHero Class Death KnightHero Class Spellblade

GLOBAL.MagicOrbWeaponConcept.name: Magic Orb Weapon
GLOBAL.MagicOrbWeaponConcept.description:
Magical artifacts that let the hero do non-physical attacks from a distance.

Usable by:Hero Class RitualistHero Class Mage

GLOBAL.MagicRangedConcept.name: Magic Ranged
GLOBAL.MagicRangedConcept.description:
Magical artifacts such as staves and magical orbs that let the hero do non-physical attacks from a distance.

Usable by:Hero Class RitualistHero Class Mage

GLOBAL.MagicStaffWeaponConcept.name: Magic Staff Weapon
GLOBAL.MagicStaffWeaponConcept.description:
Magical artifacts that let the hero do non-physical attacks from a distance. Grant the hero D E F E N S E S. W A R D I N G.

Usable by:Hero Class RitualistHero Class Mage

GLOBAL.OneHandedWeaponConcept.name: One Handed Weapon
GLOBAL.OneHandedWeaponConcept.description:
These are smaller melee weapons such as swords, maces, and daggers. They leave the left hand free to use a shield.

Usable by:Hero Class DefenderHero Class Warrior

GLOBAL.PolearmWeaponConcept.name: Polearm Weapon
GLOBAL.PolearmWeaponConcept.description:
These are long melee weapons such as spears, polearms, and glaives. They grant the hero First Strike and P R O P E R T I E S. C H A R G E_ R E S I S T A N C E.

Usable by:Hero Class DefenderHero Class WarriorHero Class Death KnightHero Class Spellblade

GLOBAL.RangedWeaponConcept.name: Ranged Weapon
GLOBAL.RangedWeaponConcept.description:
These are weapons such as bows, crossbows, and muskets. They let the hero do non-physical attacks from a distance.

Usable by:Hero Class Ranger

GLOBAL.ShieldConcept.name: Shield
GLOBAL.ShieldConcept.description:
Shields are defensive weapons that can be wielded with One Handed Weapon weapons. They grant the hero D E F E N S E S. S H I E L D_ W A L L.

Usable by:Hero Class DefenderHero Class WarriorHero Class Death KnightHero Class Spellblade

GLOBAL.SkirmishingWeaponConcept.name: Skirmisher Weapon
GLOBAL.SkirmishingWeaponConcept.description:
These are weapon pairs, such as a crossbow and dagger, that allow a hero to make both melee and ranged attacks.

Usable by:Hero Class RangerHero Class DefenderHero Class WarriorHero Class Death KnightHero Class Spellblade

GLOBAL.GreatWeaponConcept.name: Great Weapon
GLOBAL.GreatWeaponConcept.description:
These are larger melee weapons such as great swords and great axes. They grant the hero a Charge attack.

Usable by:Hero Class WarriorHero Class Death KnightHero Class Spellblade

GLOBAL.KeeperConcept.name: Keeper
GLOBAL.KeeperConcept.description:
The Race Keeper is the Leader whose Empire has the biggest presence of a race, through owned City and Pv E Vassal. You are always the Keeper of the race you start with.

To become the Keeper of a Race you need to have M I S C. R A C E_ P O P U L A T I O N_ T H R E S H O L D% of the race's Population in your Empire. If the race already has a Race Keeper you need M I S C. R A C E_ P O P U L A T I O N_ O V E R T A K E_ T H R E S H O L DPopulation more than them to take it from them.

To become the Keeper of another player's starting race the player would have to be defeated first.

The Race Keeper is the only Leader who can apply Major Race Transformation and Minor Race Transformation.

GLOBAL.LavaConcept.name: Lava
GLOBAL.LavaConcept.description:
Lava is a type of terrain that can appear both on the surface and underground. When a City annexes a Province with lava, they suffer a City Stability penalty. This penalty can be avoided by having either the Underground or Desolate Adaptation.

If the center of a province is in lava, then you will be able to build a Mine or Conduit Province Improvement.

Units that can traverse lava need to have one of the following:P R O P E R T I E S. F L Y I N G_ M O V E M E N TP R O P E R T I E S. F L O A T I N G_ M O V E M E N TP R O P E R T I E S. L A V A_ W A L K

GLOBAL.MajorRaceTransformationConcept.name: Major Race Transformation
GLOBAL.MajorRaceTransformationConcept.description:
A powerful Spell that transforms the essence of an entire race, granting powerful bonuses to all the race's units, even those not under the caster's control.
The caster must be the race's Keeper.A race can have only one Major Race Transformation at a time.

GLOBAL.MigratingConcept.name: Migrating
GLOBAL.MigratingConcept.description: Migrating a City makes it part of your Empire under your direct control, replacing its original race and culture with yours.

GLOBAL.MinorRaceTransformationConcept.name: Minor Race Transformation
GLOBAL.MinorRaceTransformationConcept.description:
A powerful Spell that transforms the essence of an entire Race, granting a bonus to all the race's units, even those not under the caster's control.
The caster must be the race's Keeper.A race can have a number of Minor Race Transformations at once.

GLOBAL.OpposingStatusEffectsConcept.name: counters
GLOBAL.OpposingStatusEffectsConcept.description:
Sometimes a status effect counters another. This means:
You can remove a status effect by applying the status effect that counters it.When a status effect counters another, it is not applied itself.

GLOBAL.AscendedTransformationConcept.name: Ascended Transformation
GLOBAL.AscendedTransformationConcept.description: Ascended transformations are Race Transformation that a Leader had when they ascended to the Pantheon Lore. The ascended transformations only apply to the Ruler (not their race) when they next appear on a realm.

GLOBAL.AscendedConcept.name: Ascended
GLOBAL.AscendedConcept.description:
An ascended Leader has proven worthy to join the Pantheon Lore and can be selected to appear as either a recruitable Hero or as Ruler.

Ascended Rulers may receive an Ascension Trait and can keep Race Transformation for when they next appear on a realm.

GLOBAL.AscensionTraitConcept.name: Ascension Trait
GLOBAL.AscensionTraitConcept.description: An ascension trait is received by a Leader upon conquering a realm. A Ruler can only have one ascension trait and can choose a trait based on the Tome they have unlocked on the realm.

GLOBAL.PillagingConcept.name: Pillaging
GLOBAL.PillagingConcept.description:
Some locations such as Province Improvement cannot be Razed but can be pillaged instead, granting Resource rewards.
When a province improvement is pillaged it is turned into Ruins.Ruins can be rebuilt at the cost of Gold.Ruins from enemy City can be Annexed to your own.

GLOBAL.PopulationConcept.name: Population
GLOBAL.PopulationConcept.description:
Population represents the size of a City. It allows the City to build new Province Improvement and expand its Domain.

Population increases with Food income and requires Population Upkeep.

GLOBAL.PopulationUpkeepConcept.name: Population Upkeep
GLOBAL.PopulationUpkeepConcept.description:
Each Population in a City costs {foodupkeep}Food and {happinessupkeep} City Stability.

Negative Food income can lead to Starvation!

GLOBAL.PrisonConcept.name: Prison
GLOBAL.PrisonConcept.description:
When you defeat an enemy Hero in combat, they have a chance of going to your prison or your Crypt.

Heroes in your prison can be granted their freedom to get their equipment and to improve relations with the Independent City or Leader they belong to.

Certain Heroes can never go to the Prison:Free City Lord cannot go to Prison, and will go to the Crypt instead.Marauder Heroes cannot go to Prison, and will go to the Crypt instead.Leader can never be captured, and will go to the Void instead.
